title: Completeness transfers to the product of two metric spaces
statement: For any two metric spaces M and N, if M and N are each `Metric.Complete` then their product `Metric.prod M N` (carried by `Sigma.{0,0} M.carrier (fun _ => N.carrier)`, distance the max metric `dist (x,y) := CReal.max (M.dist (fst x)(fst y)) (N.dist (snd x)(snd y))`) is `Metric.Complete` too. The Cauchy-ness of each projected component sequence needs no combination of moduli -- the product's own Cauchy witness already bounds both components at the same rate, via `le_max_left`/`le_max_right`. Recombining the two limits' own (independently witnessed) TendsToAt moduli into one witness for the pair DOES need a combination step: `Rat.natDivSucc` is monotone increasing in its numerator, so the SUM of the two moduli dominates both, standing in for "the max of the two moduli" (no `Nat.max` primitive is threaded through `Rat.natDivSucc`'s own lemmas; the sum has the same domination property a max would, which is the only property this proof needs).

formal.statement: theorem Metric.prod_complete : (x0 : Metric) -> (x1 : Metric) -> (x2 : Metric.Complete x0) -> (x3 : Metric.Complete x1) -> Metric.Complete (Metric.prod x0 x1)

evidence.supports: Metric.prod_complete is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, and Kernel::axiom_footprint reports 0 assumed names.

notes: WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY. It does not say Metric.cpoint (the Euclidean plane) is Metric.prod Metric.creal Metric.creal -- that pair is shown carrier-EQUIVALENT (Metric.prod_of_cpoint_of_prod / Metric.cpoint_of_prod_of_cpoint, both round trips up to each side's own equivalence), not isometric: Metric.cpoint's distance is Euclidean (sqrt of the squared distance) and Metric.prod's is the max metric built here, genuinely different formulas that are bi-Lipschitz equivalent but not equal. It also does not say Metric.cpoint is complete -- F:metric-space-completeness-of-the-real-line's own notes flagged that gap ("it needs completeness of CReal x CReal, which is not in tree"); this fact puts CReal x CReal's completeness in tree (Metric.prod Metric.creal Metric.creal, an instance of Metric.prod_complete), but closing the gap for Metric.cpoint itself still needs the missing isometry/bi-Lipschitz statement, not proved this round.
